I am a PhD student in the **School of Computer Science** at **Carnegie Mellon University** (Computational Biology Department), advised by **Dr. Jose Lugo-Martinez**.

Most recently, I led CMU's work using the [Model Hardware Standard (MHS)](posts/2026-08-27-mhs-preview.qmd) in the limited research preview: I built instrument drivers and orchestration so an AI agent could coordinate a liquid handler, plate reader, robotic arm, and cameras for closed-loop dose-response experiments. [*Nature* covered the work](https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-02990-8) on 24 September 2026.

I am seeking **Summer 2027** research and applied-science internships in agentic scientific discovery, autonomous laboratories, generative AI, reinforcement learning, and ML systems.

[[Resume (PDF)]](files/Sina_Barazandeh_Resume.pdf) · [[Academic CV (PDF)]](files/Sina_Barazandeh_CV.pdf)

## Education

  Advisor: Dr. Jose Lugo-Martinez

  Advisor: Dr. A. Ercument Cicek · Thesis: Generative Models for Generating and Optimizing Biological Sequences

## Research Highlights

- **Autonomous Laboratories / MHS:** Drivers and orchestration for a liquid handler, plate reader, robotic arm, and cameras. [Case study](posts/2026-08-27-mhs-preview.qmd)
- **Simulation & Benchmarking:** simPCL, a simulator and benchmark generator for planning and fault recovery in programmable cloud laboratories. I am interested in sim-to-real transfer, reinforcement learning in MuJoCo, and 3D world models for laboratory simulation.
- **Generative Models:** Sequence design with GANs and seq2seq models (UTRGAN, RNAtranslator, RNAGEN)
- **Reinforcement Learning:** Policy optimization for biomarker discovery under structure-aware rewards
- **ML Systems:** FlashAttention and PagedAttention in MiniTorch (LLM Systems coursework)
